chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from al-Amriki ibn Ali, from Ali ibn Ja'far, from his brother Musa, Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about a man who has the emancipation of a slave female upon him, and he wishes to free a single soul (female slave); which is better: to free an old, elderly woman or a young, unmarried one? He said: 'Free the one who enriches herself; the old, weak woman is better than the young, unmarried one.'
ai.seo_question: Which is better to free for kaffarah or voluntary emancipation: an old slave woman or a young one?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam Musa al-Kazim (AS) clarifies the merit of freeing a slave by prioritizing the elderly and weak over the young and vigorous, as their emancipation yields greater spiritual reward by removing a dependent burden. This ruling reflects the Shia juristic principle that 'fadhilah' (superiority) in manumission is measured by the degree of relief provided to the specific individual, emphasizing compassion for the vulnerable. The concept of 'aghna nafsahu' (enriching oneself) highlights how freeing those with less capacity to earn contributes more significantly to the owner's spiritual wealth.
